categories.main_business_segments: C.H. Robinson operates through two primary reportable segments: North American Surface Transportation (NAST) providing truckload and less-than-truckload (LTL) services across North America, and Global Forwarding providing ocean freight, air freight, and customs brokerage services through an international network. The company also operates Robinson Fresh (sourcing services for fresh produce), Managed Services (including Managed TMS), and Other Surface Transportation in Europe, collectively reported as All Other and Corporate.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company's core technology is Navisphere, a proprietary global multimodal transportation management system that matches customer needs with supplier capabilities, manages shipments, and provides real-time visibility. The company also operates approximately 900 data scientists, engineers, and developers creating industry-first tools including Procure IQ, Emissions IQ, and Market Rate IQ. The company leverages one of the largest freight shipment datasets in the industry combined with artificial intelligence and data-driven analytics to optimize supply chain performance.
categories.primary_customers_markets: C.H. Robinson serves more than 90,000 customers worldwide across diverse industries including Fortune 100 companies and small businesses. Primary customer types include grocery retailers, restaurants, foodservice distributors, produce wholesalers, and companies across food, beverage, retail, manufacturing, housing, paper, ecommerce, and printing industries. The company handled approximately 19 million shipments in 2023 with $22 billion of freight under management.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company operates globally with offices in North America (U.S., Canada, Mexico), Europe, Asia, Oceania, South America, and the Middle East. As of December 31, 2023, the company had 15,246 employees across 39 countries, with significant operations in North America (10,448 employees), Europe (2,068 employees), Asia and Middle East (1,928 employees), Oceania (441 employees), and South America (361 employees).
categories.supply_chain_position: C.H. Robinson operates as a midstream logistics intermediary, functioning as a service provider and broker rather than owning transportation equipment. The company arranges transportation services by connecting customers with over 450,000 contracted transportation providers including motor carriers, railroads, ocean carriers, and air carriers. The company does not employ drivers or own significant transportation equipment, instead leveraging relationships with third-party providers to fulfill customer freight requirements.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: The company's strategic priorities center on evolving constantly, delivering excellence, growing together, and embracing integrity (EDGE values). Key R&D initiatives include investing in technology and data science to develop AI-powered tools, enhance Navisphere capabilities, improve supply chain visibility and optimization, support sustainability goals through emissions tracking, and digitize customer, carrier, and internal tools. The company committed approximately 900 personnel to data science, engineering, and development roles globally.
categories.revenue_model: C.H. Robinson generates revenue primarily through transportation and logistics services (95% of adjusted gross profits in 2023), earning the difference between what customers are charged for services and what is paid to transportation providers. The company also generates revenue from sourcing services (5% of adjusted gross profits), selling fresh produce to retailers and foodservice companies. Revenue is recognized as performance obligations are satisfied, typically upon shipment completion or delivery. Most contracts are transactional or spot-market based with some prearranged contractual rates, typically for one year or less.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: C.H. Robinson competes against traditional and non-traditional logistics companies including technology-based service companies, trucking companies, property freight brokers, carriers offering logistics services, NVOCCs, IACs, and freight forwarders. The company also competes with carriers' internal sales forces and customers bringing services in-house. As one of the world's largest global logistics platforms, the company differentiates through its people and relationships, global suite of services, scale, proprietary information and technology (Navisphere), network, proven processes, and financial stability.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: C.H. Robinson is one of the largest global logistics companies with consolidated total revenues of $17.6 billion in 2023, down 28.7% from $24.7 billion in 2022 due to weak freight demand and excess carrier capacity. Adjusted gross profits decreased 27.5% to $2.6 billion in 2023. Net income declined 65.4% to $325.1 million, with diluted earnings per share of $2.72 compared to $7.40 in 2022. The company is a large accelerated filer on the Nasdaq Global Select Market with a market capitalization of approximately $10.9 billion as of June 30, 2023.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: C.H. Robinson's value proposition centers on delivering smarter supply chain solutions through its information advantage, technology expertise, and global network. The company emphasizes providing customers with improved cost reductions, reliability, sustainability visibility, and supply chain optimization. Key differentiators include knowledgeable people acting as logistics experts, a comprehensive global suite of multimodal services, industry-leading scale and capacity, proprietary data insights from 19 million annual shipments, advanced Navisphere technology with AI capabilities, and proven processes combining strategy with practical experience for customized solutions.
